newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea, facing famine, hit by drought.
newsitem.headline: North Korea, facing famine, hit by drought.

text.p: Famine-hit North Korea said on Monday that after two years of record floods, an unprecedented drought gripped the country and was severely damaging crops.
The state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo, said rivers, lakes and reservoirs in many parts of the country were drying up after a month-long hot spell.

"A long spell of drought without precedent in Korea...is having a grave effect on the growth of crops. As of July 19, hundreds of thousands of hectares of arable land had been affected by the drought," KCNA said.
The drought has struck as North Korea struggles to survive widespread famine caused by floods that devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases in 1995 and 1996.

KCNA reported major crop damage from the drought in four of North Korea's nine provinces -- North Whanghae and South Pyongyang provinces in the southwest and South Hankyong and North Hankyong provinces in the northeast.

"The damage to crops is exceptionally serious. The amount of water in rivers, lakes and reservoirs has been reduced rapidly. Not only maize and other dry-field crops but also rice stalks are withering with paddy fields becoming dry," the official news agency reported.

"The abnormal high temperature began in some areas in June and gradually spread to all other areas in July, causing the drought. In some areas, the temperature has been more than 35 degrees Celsius (95 Fahrenheit) for several days," KCNA added.
Troops had been drafted in to draw water from wells, hot springs and reservoirs to irrigate fields.
North Korea, which has long proclaimed a policy of self-reliance, has been forced to plead for foreign aid to keep alive its population until harvests in October.

Despite repeated United Nations World Food Programme appeals for aid and bilateral donations from governments and aid groups, North Korea still needed to import at least 400,000 tonnes of grain to maintain daily rations at the minimum 460 grams (one pound) until harvest time, South Korea said last week.
